newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot selects Collins avionics for its Boeings.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot selects Collins avionics for its Boeings.

text.p: Aeroflot -Russian International Airlines and U.S. Rockwell 's Avionics and Communication (A&C) signed a deal to equip 10 Boeing 737-400 jets by Collins avionics, Rockwell's office in Moscow said on Wednesday.
Collins is a division of Rockwell A&C.
"Aeroflot Chief Executive Valery Okulov and Clay Jones, executive vice president of Rockwell A&C, announced selection of the Collins avionics at the Paris Air Show," the company statement said.
Aeroflot and U.S. plane-maker Boeing Co., have signed a deal this April for the Russian flagship carrier to buy 10 737-400 passenger jets worth about $400 million.
Delivery of the jets is scheduled to begin in April 1998.

The Rockwell A&C's statement said that each of the jets would be equipped with communication, radio and sensors as well as a Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) and link management system.

It also quoted Okulov as saying that "the high reliability and time-tested operational performance of Collins avionics system entirely satisfy Aeroflot's improved requirements for flight safety in...crowded airspace".
Aeroflot was the first Russian airline to use TCAS equipping its aircraft with the system in 1994.
